spring harvest is the preferred harvest time.
the FALL treatment has the greatest biomass yield, but the highest variability.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best management practice for switchgrass on marginal land is to harvest it in late spring.
the SPRING treatment is best for maximum yield, and that the FALL treatment is best for high quality biomass.
a fall baling treatment, which is the most common practice, is the best management option for switchgrass production.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spring harvest scheme is more consistent than overwintering switchgrasses in terms of yield and quality.
switchgrass can be harvested in late fall with little yield loss and can be stored in the field with no loss for a year or more.
the SPRING harvest management scheme can be used to harvest switchgrass on marginal cropland and achieve high-quality biomass with minimal field operations.
